edbDesc: An electrical phenomenon caused when a conductor is exposed to a changing magnetic field due to relative motion of the field source and conductor; or due to variations of the field with time. This can cause eddys of circulating current within the conductor which create electromagnets with magnetic fields that opposes the change of the magnetic field.
title: Eddy currents
description: Move a magnet past a sheet of copper or aluminium and swirling currents spring up in the metal, dragging against the motion and warming it. Foucault showed in 1855 that a copper disc spun between magnet poles slows down and heats up. A magnet dropped down a copper pipe drifts down slowly as if through syrup, and the same drag stops trains and sorts drink cans.
effect: a moving or changing magnetic field stirs up swirling currents in metal that brake it and heat it
usedIn: Eddy-current brakes on trains and roller coasters
Metal detectors and coin checkers in vending machines
Recycling separators that fling aluminium cans off a conveyor
strength: A strong magnet takes several seconds to fall through a 30 cm copper pipe instead of a quarter of a second.
pickWhy: A specific effect with many uses; Faraday's induction card is the cause, but Foucault's braking and heating is a separate discovery and job.
